title: smoke_MaxPoolV8_CPU_4D primTypeCheck(primType) is unexpected (undef_f32 vs acl_f32)

failed_jobs.name: CPU functional tests / CPU functional tests

key_errors:
src/plugins/intel_cpu/tests/functional/utils/cpu_test_utils.cpp:248: Failure
Value of: primTypeCheck(primType)
  Actual: false
Expected: true
primType is unexpected : undef_f32 Expected : acl_f32
root_cause: The ARM64 cross-compiled ACL (Arm Compute Library) backend selected an undefined primitive descriptor (undef_f32) instead of the expected acl_f32 for a specific MaxPoolV8 shape/parameter combination (kernel 11x7, dynamic batch/channel dims, explicit padding). This is not related to the PR under test (NPUW pyramid attention / block-KV changes on x86-only intel_npu plugin code); the failing test belongs to the CPU plugin's ACL executor selection path on ARM64, which is known to be sensitive to specific shape/kernel combinations and has produced the same primTypeCheck assertion (with a different primitive/prim-type combo, undef vs ref) once before on 2026-07-17. This points to an intermittent/flaky primitive-selection issue in the ACL CPU executor rather than a deterministic regression introduced by this PR's NPUW-only changes.
reproduction_steps: On an ARM64 (aarch64) build with ACL enabled, run: ./ov_cpu_func_tests --gtest_filter=*smoke_MaxPoolV8_CPU_4D/MaxPoolingV8LayerCPUTest.CompareWithRefs*IS*inFmts=nhwc_outFmts=nhwc_primitive=acl* repeatedly; the primTypeCheck failure may only reproduce intermittently since it depends on ACL's internal primitive-descriptor resolution for this exact shape set.
recommended_actions: Re-run only the failed CPU functional tests job on the merge-queue run to confirm this is transient (unrelated to PR #37783's NPUW-only file changes).

If it reproduces consistently, file/triage against the CPU plugin ACL executor selection code (src/plugins/intel_cpu/src/nodes/executors/acl/*) for the MaxPoolV8 op with kernel {11,7}, dynamic input shapes, and explicit padding.
Consider adding this specific parameter combination to the ARM64 known-issues/skip list if it is confirmed as a pre-existing flaky case unrelated to any recent PR.
prevention_strategies: Add CI-level tracking/quarantine for intermittently-failing ACL primitive-selection tests on ARM64 so a single flaky assertion does not block unrelated merge-queue entries; consider stabilizing ACL primitive-type resolution logic for edge-case pooling parameter combinations.
historical_context: A near-identical assertion (primTypeCheck(primType) is unexpected) was previously recorded on 2026-07-17 for smoke_ConvertCPULayerTest with primType unknown vs ref, categorized as Flaky Test (pattern 76751669c7a78fcd, count 1). This occurrence involves a different op (MaxPoolV8) and prim-type pair (undef_f32 vs acl_f32), so it is tracked as a new, related-but-distinct pattern (eb0b94c864ee1a85) rather than merged into the prior one, since the normalized error text differs.
